drugs.name: Aminoglycosides (amikacin, streptomycin, gentamicin)
drugs.mechanism: Irreversible 30S binding blocks initiation and causes mRNA misreading; the only bactericidal protein synthesis inhibitors; concentration-dependent killing and a post-antibiotic effect allow 48-72 h dosing
drugs.adverseEffects: Nephrotoxicity (nonoliguric acute tubular necrosis; follow BUN and creatinine); ototoxicity of hearing and balance, worse with loop diuretics or cisplatin; neuromuscular blockade in myasthenia; fetal CN VIII damage
drugs.use: Parenteral second-line drug for MDR-TB; plague and tularemia; with ampicillin for a neonatal UTI; added for gram-negative cover in severe HAP; synergy with a beta-lactam against S. aureus

drugs.name: Fluoroquinolones (moxifloxacin, levofloxacin, ciprofloxacin)
drugs.mechanism: Block DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV, so supercoiled DNA cannot relax and reseal; bactericidal. Resistance: altered gyrase, reduced uptake. Inhibit CYP1A2; chelated by antacids, iron and dairy
drugs.adverseEffects: QT prolongation; tendon rupture (older adults, rheumatoid arthritis, glucocorticoids); damage to growing cartilage, so avoided in children and pregnancy; photosensitivity; raise theophylline levels
drugs.use: MDR-TB and the newer 4-month TB regimen; 'respiratory' agents for CAP with comorbidities or admission; anthrax; drug of choice for bacterial prostatitis (2-4 weeks); 3-day course for cystitis

drugs.name: Ethionamide
drugs.mechanism: Blocks mycolic acid synthesis like the first-line cell-wall prodrug, but is activated by the EthA enzyme rather than katG catalase-peroxidase
drugs.use: Second-line TB drug that can still work after isoniazid fails because of a katG mutation

drugs.name: Cycloserine
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits alanine racemase (L-alanine to D-alanine), the cell-wall step before the D-Ala-D-Ala stage; also inhibits GABA transaminase and acts as a partial NMDA agonist
drugs.adverseEffects: Neurologic toxicity: enhanced excitatory glutamate signaling from partial NMDA agonism can provoke seizures; the neurologic effects limit its use

drugs.name: Linezolid
drugs.mechanism: Binds the 50S subunit (23S rRNA) to block protein synthesis; resistance from a 23S rRNA gene mutation; 100% oral bioavailability, so IV and oral doses are interchangeable
drugs.adverseEffects: Weak MAO inhibition: serotonin syndrome with SSRIs or other serotonergic drugs; bone marrow suppression from impaired mitochondrial ATP production
drugs.use: VRE, MRSA (including MRSA HAP/VAP as the alternative to vancomycin) and penicillin-resistant pneumococcus; the third drug of BPaL for MDR/XDR-TB
